title: Madrid Essentials
description: Everything you need before you arrive and during your stay — visas, money, transport (metro, buses, airport, trains), tourist information (maps, apps, SIM cards, WiFi), Spanish language, and safety. The practical foundation for your Madrid visit.

subcategories.title: Visas & Entry
subcategories.summary: Visa requirements and entry rules: Schengen visas, UK & USA citizen guides, long-stay visas, residency permits, and USA-specific provisions (FATCA, driver's license, Digital Nomad Visa). Original 2014 site: Work & Residency → Visa: UK, Visa: USA, USA Citizens in Spain.
subcategories.tips: EU/EEA citizens: no visa required, but register for residency if staying >90 days. Non-EU tourists: Schengen 90/180 rule applies. Long-stay (study, work, family reunification): apply at the Spanish consulate in your home country BEFORE arriving. USA citizens: see the USA Citizens guide for FATCA, driver's license, and Digital Nomad Visa specifics.

subcategories.title: Money & Budgets
subcategories.summary: Money and budgets: cost of living, ATMs, currency exchange, cards, tipping, and tax refunds. Original 2014 site: Gen Info → Banks (banking moved to Living → Banking).
subcategories.tips: ATMs (cajeros automáticos) are everywhere — use bank ATMs (not Euronet) to avoid fees. Credit cards widely accepted except at small bars. Tip 5–10% at restaurants if service was good. Non-EU tourists can claim VAT (IVA) refund on purchases over €90.16 — ask for the tax-free form.

subcategories.title: Getting Around Madrid
subcategories.summary: Getting around WITHIN Madrid: metro, Cercanías commuter rail, city buses, night buses, taxis, ride-sharing (Uber/Cabify), BiciMAD e-bikes, e-scooters, walking, driving, parking, and transit maps. Original 2014 site: Travel → Metro Madrid, Buses (Local), Taxis, Driving.
subcategories.tips: Metro is the fastest way around (€1.50–2.00 single, €12.20 for 10 trips). A 10-trip Metrobús card works on metro AND buses. Night buses (Búhos) run from Cibeles after Metro closes. BiciMAD e-bikes (€0.50/30 min) are great for short hops. Cercanías commuter rail connects suburbs to city center (€1.70–4.50). For intercity travel (AVE, Renfe, buses to other cities), see Intercity Travel from Madrid.

subcategories.title: Intercity Travel from Madrid
subcategories.summary: Leaving Madrid: AVE high-speed trains, Renfe national trains, Eurail/Interrail passes, intercity buses & coaches, coach stations, and Madrid's major transit hubs (Atocha, Chamartín). Original 2014 site: Travel → Airport, Buses: Madrid to..., Trains, Eurail Passes.
subcategories.tips: AVE high-speed trains: Madrid→Toledo 30 min, Madrid→Sevilla 2.5 hr, Madrid→Barcelona 2.5 hr. Book early at renfe.com (€20–80). Intercity buses from Estación Sur (Méndez Álvaro) are cheaper but slower. Atocha serves south/east; Chamartín serves north. Eurail/Interrail passes require seat reservations (€10–35 per AVE trip).

subcategories.title: Madrid-Barajas Airport
subcategories.summary: Madrid-Barajas Airport (MAD): terminals, airlines, shuttle services, information desks, left luggage, delays, and strikes. Original 2014 site: Travel → Airport, Airport Shuttle Service, Major Airlines.
subcategories.tips: Metro Line 8 (€5) connects all terminals to city center in 15 min. Airport Express Bus (€5, 24h) runs to Atocha. Taxi flat rate €30 to city center (Zone A). For door-to-door shuttles, book in advance (€25–40). Check Barajas Delays for current disruptions.

subcategories.title: Spanish Language
subcategories.summary: Survival Spanish for visitors: essential phrases for restaurants, emergencies, and getting around. Original 2014 site: not a separate section (phrases were scattered across pages). For full language courses and schools, see Living → Education.
subcategories.tips: Learn these 20 phrases before you arrive — they cover 80% of tourist interactions. For restaurant-specific vocabulary, see Restaurant Spanish. For emergencies, see Emergency Spanish. For full language programs, see Living → Education → Language Learning.

subcategories.title: Safety & Emergencies
subcategories.summary: Safety and emergencies: emergency numbers, local police stations, embassies, tourist help, and crime/scam warnings. Original 2014 site: Gen Info → Embassies, Emergencies, Local Police Stations.
subcategories.tips: Emergency number: 112 (works for all services, English available). For non-emergencies: Policía Municipal 092, Guardia Civil 062. US Embassy: Calle Diego de León 16 (Metro Diego de León). Watch for pickpockets on Metro Line 1, Plaza Mayor, and El Rastro flea market.

subcategories.title: Tourist Information
subcategories.summary: Tourist offices, Madrid Card, official apps, internet cafés, satellite TV, left luggage, connectivity (SIM/eSIM/WiFi), and city maps. Original 2014 site: Sightseeing → Tourist Offices, Madrid Card; Shops → Internet Centers, Satellite TV, Baggage Storage.
subcategories.tips: Start at the Plaza Mayor Tourist Office (free maps, English advice, 9:30am–8:30pm daily). The Madrid Card bundles transport + museums + bus tour. For connectivity: get an eSIM (Airalo, $5 for 1GB) before landing. Free public WiFi: "Madrid_Free_WiFi" network (600+ hotspots).

title: Living in Madrid
description: Settling in Madrid for the long term — housing, bureaucracy, banking, healthcare, work, education, and the practical services you need for daily life. For expats, students, and long-term visitors.

subcategories.title: Housing
subcategories.summary: Accommodation: hostels, hotels, apart-hotels, furnished rooms, landlords, DIY flat-hunting guide, booking services, and relocation help. Original 2014 site: Accommodation section.
subcategories.tips: November–December is the best time to flat-hunt (lowest prices, most availability); September is the worst (students return, prices spike). For short stays (<1 week), hostels and apart-hotels are cheapest. For 1+ weeks, furnished room booking services beat hotel rates. For long-term, use Idealista/Fotocasa — but expect to pay 2 months deposit + 1 month agency fee.

subcategories.title: Bureaucracy
subcategories.summary: Bureaucracy: NIE/TIE (foreigner ID), empadronamiento (local registration), social security number, taxes (Modelo 720 for foreign assets), and residency permits. Original 2014 site: not a separate section (scattered across Work & Residency).
subcategories.tips: Get your NIE first — you need it for everything (bank, phone, job, rent). Apply at the Extranjería office; book an appointment online (citas.sre.gob.es). Empadronamiento at your district town hall (free, required for healthcare and schools). Modelo 720: if you have >€50k in foreign assets, you MUST declare it annually (penalty up to €1,500 for missing the deadline).

subcategories.title: Banking
subcategories.summary: Banking in Madrid: opening accounts, Spanish vs digital banks (N26, Revolut), transfers, and cards. Original 2014 site: Gen Info → Banks.
subcategories.tips: Bankinter offers an online account you can open with just a passport (no residency card needed). For everyday use, N26 and Revolut have better apps and English support. For rent and bills, you'll need a Spanish account. SEPA transfers within EU are free; international transfers cost €15–40.

subcategories.title: Healthcare
subcategories.summary: Healthcare: English-speaking doctors, hospitals, dentists, pharmacies, immunizations, public vs private system, and travel health. Original 2014 site: Health & Medical section.
subcategories.tips: EU citizens: bring your EHIC card for free public healthcare. Non-EU: travel insurance is essential (public healthcare is not free without it). For English-speaking doctors, see the Doctors group. 24-hour pharmacies: look for the rotating "farmacia de guardia" — canaldefarmacia.com shows which one is open near you.

subcategories.title: Work
subcategories.summary: Work in Madrid: English teaching, aupair, internships, journalism, hostess/promo work, freelancing, and job search. Original 2014 site: Work & Residency section.
subcategories.tips: English teaching is the easiest entry point — see English Teacher Agencies. For internships, Eurointerns and Hot English Magazine place English speakers. Aupair positions are advertised on aupairworld.com. For freelancing (autónomo), budget €280/month in social security plus accountant fees.

subcategories.title: Education
subcategories.summary: Schools, universities, language learning, libraries, teacher training, and study-abroad programs. Original 2014 site: Study & Student Life section.
subcategories.tips: For Spanish language schools, look for Cervantes Institute accreditation. The EOI (Escuela Oficial de Idiomas) is the cheapest option (€200/year) but registration is in September. For children, bilingual schools start at age 3. For language exchanges (free practice with locals), see Language Learning → Language Exchanges.

subcategories.title: Practical Services
subcategories.summary: Practical everyday services for residents: post office (Correos), launderettes, locksmiths, moving, barbers, meeting rooms, architects, translators, and religion/faith communities. Original 2014 site: Gen Info → Post Office, Religions; Shops → Launderettes, Locksmiths, Moving, Barbers, Meeting Rooms, Translating, Architect.
subcategories.tips: Post office (Correos) branches are everywhere — the largest is at Plaza de Cibeles. For left luggage, see Essentials → Tourist Info. For retail stores (electronics, music, optical, books), see Do → Shopping. For food stores (supermarkets, international grocery, health food), see Do → Food.

title: See in Madrid
description: What to see in Madrid — world-class museums (Prado, Reina Sofía, Thyssen), royal sites (Palace, Almudena, El Escorial), parks, plazas, neighborhoods, live spectator sports, live performances (theater, opera, jazz, flamenco, cinema), and family attractions (zoo, aquarium, planetarium). For guided tours and day trips, see Do → Tours & Day Trips.

subcategories.title: Museums
subcategories.summary: Museums: the Golden Triangle (Prado, Reina Sofía, Thyssen) plus kid museums, specialty museums, and current exhibitions. Original 2014 site: Arts & Entertainment → Museums → El Prado, Reina Sofia, Thyssen.
subcategories.tips: Buy the Paseo del Arte ticket (€30.40) for all three Golden Triangle museums — saves money and skips queues. Prado: free entry Mon–Sat 6–8pm, Sun 5–7pm. Reina Sofía: free Mon–Wed and Fri–Sat 7–9pm, Sun 1:30–7pm. Thyssen: free Monday 12–4pm. All three are walkable from Atocha.

subcategories.title: Royal & Historic
subcategories.summary: Royal Madrid: Royal Palace, Almudena Cathedral, Plaza de Oriente, Sabatini Gardens, Campo del Moro, and Royal Theater (Teatro Real). Original 2014 site: Sightseeing → Places of Interest (royal buildings).
subcategories.tips: Royal Palace: €12, free last 2 hours Wed. Changing of the guard: Wed 11am (small), first Wed of month 12pm (solemn). Almudena Cathedral: free entry. Sabatini Gardens: best palace photo spot at sunset. Teatro Real: opera tickets €20–200.

subcategories.title: Parks & Outdoors
subcategories.summary: Parks, gardens, and outdoor spaces: Retiro, Casa de Campo, Madrid Río, Parque del Oeste, El Capricho, Crystal Palace Arganzuela, Estufa Fría, and the Teleférico cable car. Original 2014 site: Sightseeing → Parks, Gardens, etc.; Teleferico (Sky Lift).
subcategories.tips: Retiro is the centerpiece — rowing lake, Crystal Palace, Rose Garden. Casa de Campo is huge (take the Teleférico from Argüelles to get there). El Capricho is a hidden gem (only open weekends). Madrid Río is the renovated riverfront — great for running and cycling.

subcategories.title: Plazas & Landmarks
subcategories.summary: Plazas, landmarks, and monuments: Plaza Mayor, Puerta del Sol, Plaza de Cibeles, Plaza de Colón, Puerta de Alcalá, Royal Palace, Almudena Cathedral, and Gran Vía. Original 2014 site: Sightseeing → Places of Interest.
subcategories.tips: Walk the Art Walk (Paseo del Prado) from Plaza de Cibeles to Atocha — passes the fountains, Plaza de Neptuno, and all three Golden Triangle museums. Plaza Mayor at night is magical. Royal Palace: €12 entry, free last 2 hours of Wednesday. Puerta de Alcalá is best photographed at sunset from Calle Alcalá.

subcategories.title: Neighborhoods
subcategories.summary: Madrid's barrios: Sol & Gran Vía (city center), Malasaña (hipster), Chueca (LGBTQ+), La Latina (tapas), Salamanca (luxury), Lavapiés (multicultural), Chamberí (residential), Retiro (parks & museums), and more. Original 2014 site: Sightseeing → Cool Neighborhoods; Gen Info → Areas / Barrios.
subcategories.tips: Start at Sol & Gran Vía for the classic tourist center. Malasaña for vintage shops and indie bars. Chueca for nightlife and shopping. La Latina for Sunday tapas at Cava Baja. Salamanca for luxury shopping on Calle Serrano. Lavapiés for Indian food and street art.

subcategories.title: Live Sports & Spectator Events
subcategories.summary: Live sports events: Real Madrid & Santiago Bernabéu, Atlético Madrid & Metropolitano, Rayo Vallecano, ACB basketball (Estudiantes, Real Madrid), and Madrid Open tennis. Original 2014 site: Sports & Recreation (some spectator events noted).
subcategories.tips: Real Madrid tickets: from €30 at realmadrid.com. Atlético: from €25 at clubatleticodemadrid.com. Bernabéu tour: €25 (includes stadium, trophies, tunnel). Madrid Open tennis (May): €30–200. ACB basketball: €15–40 at the Palacio de Deportes.

subcategories.title: Live Performances
subcategories.summary: Live performances: flamenco, theater (live + alternative), magic & comedy, version original cinemas, outdoor summer movies, and IMAX. Original 2014 site: Arts & Entertainment → Flamenco Shows, Live Theater, Alternative Theater, Magic & Comedy, Movies (VO + Outdoor), IMAX.
subcategories.tips: For authentic flamenco, Casa Patas and Cardamomo are the standards. For English-language theater, check the Madrid Players. Version Original (V.O.) cinemas show films in original English with Spanish subtitles — Cinesa Manoteras, Yelmo Cines Ideal, Cine Doré (€2.50).

subcategories.title: Zoos, Aquariums & Kid Museums
subcategories.summary: Zoos, aquariums, and kid museums: Zoo Aquarium de Madrid, IMAX & Planetarium, Wax Museum, Train Museum, and Science Museum. Original 2014 site: Socializing → Zoo / Aquarium; Arts → IMAX.
subcategories.tips: Zoo Aquarium: €28 adult, €21 child (combined ticket with Parque de Atracciones saves €10). IMAX/Planetarium: €8 adult, €6 child (Spanish narration mostly). Wax Museum (Museo de Cera): €12, fun for kids. Train Museum (Museo del Ferrocarril): free, weekends have mini-train rides.

title: Do in Madrid
description: What to do in Madrid — eat and drink (tapas, vermouth), go out (bars, clubs, rooftops, spas), play sports (tennis, padel, golf, swimming), take tours (walking, food, wine, Segway, day trips), shop, experience traditions (festivals, retreats), enjoy theme parks and camps with kids, and learn arts (acting, film, dance, music, writing).

subcategories.title: Food & Tapas
subcategories.summary: Food & tapas: restaurants by cuisine (Japanese, vegetarian, cheap eats, ice cream), food markets, grocery stores (supermarkets, international, health food), culinary education, and outdoor dining. Original 2014 site: Socializing → Food → Cheap Eats, Japanese, Tapas, Ice Cream; Health → Vegetarian, Health Food Stores.
subcategories.tips: Start at Mercado de San Miguel for tapas culture (touristy but iconic). For cheap eats, see Cheap Eats (under €12) — El Tigre, 100 Montaditos, Maoz. For grocery: Mercadona (best value), El Corte Inglés (premium). For international/health food, see Grocery & Food Stores group.

subcategories.title: Arts Education
subcategories.summary: Arts education: film schools, music programs, flamenco dance intensives, acting, art/design schools, architecture programs, art history courses, film industry resources, and talent agencies. Original 2014 site: Study → Film & Theater; Work → Film Resources, Talent Agencies.
subcategories.tips: For flamenco dance intensives, see Flamenco Dance Intensives. For film schools, see Film Resources (ECAM, TAI, Séptima Ars). For Spanish culture and art history courses (English-taught), see Arts Education group. For talent/modeling agencies, see Talent Agencies (Kailash, Exclusive Management).

subcategories.title: Nightlife
subcategories.summary: Nightlife: bars & cafés, nightclubs & dancing, salsa, terraces & rooftop bars, casinos, and live music venues. Original 2014 site: Socializing → Drinks → Bars/Cafés/Cocktails, Terraces; Dancing → Night Clubs, Salsa; Casinos & Gambling.
subcategories.tips: Madrid nightlife starts LATE — dinner at 10pm, bars at midnight, clubs at 2am. For tapas + drinks, La Latina (Cava Baja). For clubs, Malasaña (indie) or Chueca (electronic). For rooftops, Azotea del Círculo de Bellas Artes (€5 entry, best sunset view).

subcategories.title: Active Sports
subcategories.summary: Active sports you can DO in Madrid: gyms, yoga, cycling, boating, bowling, golf, pool, ice skating, skiing, swimming, tennis, race karts, running, cricket, rugby, and hammams/baths. Original 2014 site: Sports & Recreation (16 sports); Health → Health Clubs, Yoga; Socializing → Baths.
subcategories.tips: For drop-in sports, Madrid Río has free outdoor gyms and courts. Retiro park: free tennis courts (book at delegaciondeportes.madrid.es). BiciMAD for cycling. For hammams, Hammam Al Ándalus (€40–80, 5 min from Plaza Mayor). Skiing: Navacerrada and Valdesquí are 1 hr by bus.

subcategories.title: Training Camps & Certification
subcategories.summary: Training camps & certification programs: soccer, tennis, golf, basketball, volleyball, cycling, running (altitude), skiing, yoga (YTT), pilates, and fitness instructor courses. Original 2014 site: not a separate section (training programs scattered across Sports).
subcategories.tips: Real Madrid & Atlético run summer soccer camps (€300–600/week, ages 6–17). Tennis academies: Equelite (Sánchez-Casal), €800/week residential. YTT (Yoga Teacher Training): Sivananda €2,000–4,000 for 200-hour certification. Most camps are English-friendly for international students.

subcategories.title: Tours & Day Trips
subcategories.summary: Tours & day trips: walking tours, bus tours, bike tours, food tours, SEG tours, day trips to Toledo/Segovia/Ávila/El Escorial, and the Camino de Santiago. Original 2014 site: Sightseeing → Tours → Bus Tours, Walking/SEG Tours, Other Tours.
subcategories.tips: Free walking tours (tip-based) start at Plaza Mayor daily at 11am and 2pm. For day trips: Toledo (30 min by AVE), Segovia (30 min by AVE), El Escorial (1 hr by bus). Book AVE early at renfe.com for €20 fares. Devour Madrid food tours are the best English-language option.

subcategories.title: Shopping
subcategories.summary: Shopping: luxury (Calle Serrano), flea markets (El Rastro), specialty shops (bookstores, computer/electronics, music, optical), and shopping areas. Original 2014 site: Shops & Services → Shops/Stores → Book Stores, Computer Stores, Music Stores, Optical Shops.
subcategories.tips: For luxury shopping, head to Calle Serrano (Salamanca district). For unique finds, El Rastro flea market is Sunday mornings only. For English-language books, see Bookstores group. For food markets, see Do → Food → Markets & Food Halls.

subcategories.title: Madrid Culture
subcategories.summary: Madrid traditions & culture: bullfighting (Las Ventas), flamenco shows, Spanish customs, festivals (San Isidro, Verbenas), folk dance (Chotis), and monastery/meditation retreats. Original 2014 site: Arts & Entertainment → Bullfights; Gen Info → Spanish Culture.
subcategories.tips: Bullfighting season: May–October at Las Ventas (Sundays). San Isidro festival (May) is the biggest bullfighting event. For flamenco as performance (watching), see See → Live Performances. For flamenco dance intensives (learning), see Do → Arts Education.

subcategories.title: Theme Parks & Active Family Fun
subcategories.summary: Family fun: theme parks (Parque de Atracciones, Warner Park), water parks (Aquópolis, Warner Beach), family shows, and English-language summer camps. Original 2014 site: Socializing → Theme Parks, Water Parks.
subcategories.tips: Parque de Atracciones: €35 adult, €28 child (Metro Casa de Campo). Warner Park: €45 (50 km south, shuttle from Méndez Álvaro). Aquópolis: €28 (San Fernando de Henares). For zoos/kid museums, see See → Zoos & Kid Museums.

title: Madrid Now
description: What is happening in Madrid right now — this week's events, open exhibitions, English-language news, and live info (time, weather, UV, pollen). Updated regularly. Featured on the homepage.

subcategories.title: Events
subcategories.summary: This week's events — festivals, concerts, cultural events, food festivals.
subcategories.tips: Major annual events: San Isidro (May 11-15), Madrid Pride (June-July), Veranos de la Villa (July-August), PhotoEspaña (June-July), Mad Cool music festival (July). For daily listings: esMadrid.com (official, English), Madrid Secreto (Spanish, hidden events). Many events are free — check the esMadrid app.

subcategories.title: Exhibitions
subcategories.summary: Current exhibitions at Prado, Reina Sofía, Thyssen, Matadero, Mapfre, CaixaForum.
subcategories.tips: Museum exhibitions rotate every 3-4 months. Check museum websites for current shows. Matadero Madrid (contemporary art, free) and CaixaForum (€6) have the most rotating exhibitions. PhotoEspaña (June-July) brings photography to 70+ venues. Many museums have free entry times — see our individual museum records.

subcategories.title: News
subcategories.summary: English-language news, radio, publications, magazines, and expat message boards for Madrid. Original 2014 site: Arts & Entertainment → Radio (English); Gen Info → Publications, Message Boards.
subcategories.tips: For daily news: The Local (thelocal.es), Madrid Metropolitan (monthly magazine). For radio: Madrid Live (100.4 FM, Tuesdays 6:30pm). For expat message boards: Madrid Man, Multimadrid (older but active forums). For job classifieds: Loquo, Lingobongo.

subcategories.title: Right Now
subcategories.summary: Live info — current Madrid time, weather, UV index, air quality, pollen count, sunrise/sunset.
subcategories.tips: Madrid time: CET (UTC+1) winter, CEST (UTC+2) summer. Summer UV reaches 10+ — wear sunscreen May-September. Summer heat: 35-40°C July-August, avoid outdoor activity 2-5pm. Pollen: olive (May-June) is worst — check SEAIC daily count. Best sunset spot: Temple of Debod (arrive 30-45 min before). Air quality: generally good, NO2 can spike in winter.
